finding.title: Split the 6 gamification test files that exceed the 400-line AG-3 cap
finding.why: docs/coding-standards.md:512 states oversized files 'exceed per-file agent read budgets... become dumping grounds.' reward_config_controller_test.dart at 1041 lines is 2.6x the 400-line cap; content past an agent's read window is effectively invisible on future edits/audits.
finding.recommendation: Split each file along its existing group() boundaries (e.g. reward_config_controller_test.dart's 22 numbered groups) into separate files per concern, mirroring how the smaller staleness/reactive/overflow regression tests already live as separate files.
acceptance_criteria: `find lib test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'` (the checker named in docs/coding-standards.md:513) reports none of these 6 files.

finding.title: Introduce test/helpers/pump_app.dart — 6 gamification test files hand-roll near-identical MaterialApp/ProviderScope boilerplate
finding.why: docs/coding-standards.md:462-465 (TQ-3) names `test/helpers/pump_app.dart` as 'the reviewed convention' for this exact ProviderScope+localization-delegate boilerplate, but the file doesn't exist anywhere in the repo (confirmed via ls test/helpers/). In this batch alone, child_redemption_screen_l1_test.dart (_pumpScreen + _pumpScreenWithRouter), gamification_screen_l1_test.dart (_buildApp), parent_pending_redemptions_screen_l1_test.dart (_buildScreen + buildWithRouter), reward_configuration_screen_l1_test.dart (_buildFake), streak_widget_test.dart (buildWidget) and achievement_unlock_celebration_test.dart (_buildHarness) each reimplement the same ~20-30 line scaffold independently; achievement_unlock_celebration_test.dart even duplicates its own _buildHarness body inline twice (lines 272-294 and 297-319) instead of calling it, showing the drift risk in practice — any future fix to the shared scaffold (e.g. a new required delegate) must be hand-applied at every site.
finding.recommendation: Create test/helpers/pump_app.dart per the standards doc and migrate these builders to call it, parameterizing only the feature-specific overrides.
acceptance_criteria: The 6 cited builder functions delegate to it instead of duplicating MaterialApp/localizationsDelegates/ProviderScope setup.

finding.title: Wire or remove the no-op profileMode parameter on reward_config_controller_test.dart's _makeContainer
finding.rule: TQ-7-adjacent (test helper must do what its doc comment claims)

evidence.quote: /// Pass [profileMode] as 'child' or 'adult' to test profile-type branching.

finding.why: _makeContainer's doc comment promises profileMode drives 'profile-type branching' overrides, but the function body only ever reads profileId — profileMode is accepted and silently discarded. The one call site that passes profileMode: 'adult' (in the 'product rule: adults have no points' test) gets zero behavioral effect from it; a future test adding profileMode: 'child' expecting a different container wiring would get a false pass.
finding.recommendation: Either delete the unused parameter, or wire it to an actual profile-mode override (e.g. a stubbed profileModeProvider) so it matches its doc comment.
acceptance_criteria: _makeContainer's profileMode parameter is either removed or demonstrably changes container behavior, with a test asserting the difference between 'adult' and 'child'.

finding.title: Replace fixed-duration Future.delayed sleeps with deterministic sync in gamification reactive-stream tests
finding.why: These 3 files (10 occurrences total) use hard-coded 20/50/150ms real-time sleeps as the only synchronization before asserting a Drift Stream has propagated a new emission, with no retry/poll and no use of pumpEventQueue() (confirmed 0 usages repo-wide). On a loaded CI runner a slower-than-budgeted FFI round-trip would fail the assertion with no code regression involved — exactly the kind of flake that erodes trust in the 'staleness regression' suite meant to guard DG-RDMP-01/02 and DG-PND-05.
finding.recommendation: Replace `Future.delayed(fixedDuration)` with `pumpEventQueue()` or a small poll-until-condition helper bounded by a generous timeout, so the wait tracks actual event-loop drain rather than a guessed duration.
acceptance_criteria: No test in these 3 files gates its only assertion on a bare Future.delayed(fixed duration); a poll/pumpEventQueue-based helper is used instead.

finding.title: Fix stale 'flagged as BUG (no UI lock)' header comment in parent_pending_redemptions_screen_l1_test.dart
finding.rule: Documentation must not contradict the code/tests it sits beside

evidence.quote: ///   - Double-tap guard: tapping Approve twice — flagged as BUG (no UI lock).
// guard: _RedemptionCard disables Fulfil/Decline (_busy) while the async is

finding.why: The file's own header (line 12) claims Approve double-tap is an open, un-guarded bug, but parent_pending_redemptions_screen.dart:199-207/263/286 has a `_busy` flag disabling both Fulfil and Decline while an operation is in flight, and this same test file's later comment (lines 588-594) correctly describes that guard. A maintainer skimming only the header would believe there's live unfixed work here or file a duplicate bug report.
finding.recommendation: Update the header bullet to describe the _busy guard instead of the stale 'flagged as BUG' claim, matching lines 588-594.
acceptance_criteria: Header comment at the top of the file no longer claims an unguarded double-tap bug on Approve.
